published.citation: Alonso et al. 2010, dayside brightness temperature at 2.15 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 1890 +/- 350 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010AJ....139.1481A/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 2.15 µm (Isaac Newton Group (ING) 4.2m William Herschel Telescope (WHT) at Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos LIRIS) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 1 measured of 6 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: Isaac Newton Group (ING) 4.2m William Herschel Telescope (WHT) at Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos LIRIS
